reading.body:
Lovo is a voice cloning and synthesis company whose only listed product, Genny, is built around consent and disclosure rules for synthetic media.

The data covers one product in one category, Voice and Audio. It records that the product handles likeness consent, commercial voiceover, and synthetic media disclosure, which places the company in the part of the AI stack that generates speech rather than the part that trains models.

Voice synthesis is a compute consumer at inference time, not a builder of data centers. Nothing here describes how much compute Lovo buys, where it runs, or what power contracts sit behind it. The listing also carries an unrelated MCP entry for a different service, Lovora, which is not part of this company's product line.

What the data does not tell the reader is scale. There are no customer counts, revenue figures, model sizes, or infrastructure details, so no claim can be made about Lovo's footprint in the grid or its weight in the AI buildout.
